cf.title: A bug in recovery prefetcher, triggering asserts / FATAL: checkpoint request failed

input.subject: A bug in recovery prefetcher, triggering asserts / FATAL: checkpoint request failed

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The thread states the bug, its two failure modes and the fix, and three people confirmed the fix in messages #2 to #4. The patch clears one field of the prefetcher's private state and adds no user-visible surface. Confidence is medium because the code was not read and the claim about the other callers rests on the commit message.

brief.title: Clear stale prefetcher record in XLogPrefetcherBeginRead to fix recovery end
brief.problem: XLogPrefetcherBeginRead resets the prefetcher queue but keeps prefetcher->record, so FinishWalRecovery can fail to re-read the last replayed record when recovery stops at a recovery target. Assert builds then crash, and other builds write a wrong timeline switch point and fail with "FATAL: checkpoint request failed". The bug affects Postgres 15 and later, mostly with maintenance_io_concurrency set to 7 or less.
brief.proposed_design: The patch sets prefetcher->record to NULL in XLogPrefetcherBeginRead, so the next read decodes the record at the new position. A new TAP test stops recovery just before a multi-block XLOG_FPI record from an SP-GiST index build, with maintenance_io_concurrency = 1. The fix is backpatched through 15.
author_claims: The bug has existed since Postgres 15.
On non-assert builds the new timeline history file gets a wrong switch point, and a restart replays WAL past the recovery target.
It triggers when maintenance_io_concurrency is 7 or less and the recovery target is shortly before a bulk XLOG_FPI record.
The other callers of XLogPrefetcherBeginRead run before the redo loop, so they never have a current record.
The TAP test works unchanged in back branches 15 to 18.
brief.thread_state: Chao Li, shihao zhong and Surya Poondla tested or reviewed the fix and agree with it. Surya suggests a separate patch that makes FinishWalRecovery PANIC if the last record cannot be re-read; whether to keep the TAP test is still open.
unclear: The author is not sure the bug needs reduced maintenance_io_concurrency, and nobody shows a case with the default setting.
The thread does not say whether to commit the TAP test or keep it only as a reproducer.
The material does not say how existing clusters with a wrong timeline switch point can be detected or repaired.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The fix changes xlogprefetcher.c, which runs in the startup process and decides where WAL ends at a recovery target.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The commit message asks for a backpatch through 15, with a TAP test written to run unchanged in 15 to 18.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The patch adds a new recovery TAP test, 061_recovery_target_prefetch.pl, that depends on the WAL pattern of an SP-GiST index build.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Can the bug occur with the default maintenance_io_concurrency, for example with a record that has enough block references that need I/O?
Should the TAP test be committed and backpatched, or kept only as a reproducer?
How can a user detect and repair a cluster whose timeline history file already has a wrong switch point from this bug?
Should a separate patch make FinishWalRecovery fail loudly when it cannot re-read the last replayed record?

committability.owner_note: The CommitFest entry lists Tomas Vondra as author and the commit message carries a backpatch line; the owner needs to know the WAL replay and recovery prefetcher code.
committability.liability: A change to recovery-end behaviour in four or more back branches, plus a TAP test that must stay stable on the buildfarm in each of them.
committability.author_follow_up: The author found the bug while working on other recovery prefetcher improvements, which suggests continued work in this area; the thread has no explicit statement.

priority.reason: The bug needs a recovery target shortly before a bulk XLOG_FPI record and mostly maintenance_io_concurrency of 7 or less, but the result is a wrong timeline switch point and replay past the target. The fix is one pointer reset in one file, and three people confirmed it.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the claim that the other callers of XLogPrefetcherBeginRead never have a current record is unchecked. The stability of the TAP test across branches and buildfarm animals could not be judged.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Be strict when request to flush past end of WAL in WaitXLogInsertionsToFinish
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread first proposed raising the "request to flush past end of generated WAL" message in WaitXLogInsertionsToFinish() from LOG to PANIC. It later moved to a patch that makes XLogBackgroundFlush() honor the adjusted (clamped) return value instead of discarding it, plus a TAP test that reproduces the header-only flush that broke replay on a standby.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was not rejected on its merits. Bharath Rupireddy created commitfest entry #7294 without knowing the author had already registered #7252 for the same thread. The author asked for #7294 to be withdrawn so the history stays in one entry, and it was withdrawn on the same day.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Could you withdraw #7294 so we don't split the history between two entries?

precedents_retrieved.title: I thought it would be better to add a POSIx_fadvise description for the recovery_prefetch parameter here, to distinguish it from the database functions.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The entry proposes adding a description of posix_fadvise to the documentation of the recovery_prefetch parameter, to set it apart from database functions. It is attached to the WAL prefetch thread, where recovery reads ahead in the WAL and calls PrefetchBuffer() for referenced blocks, which relies on POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. None of the shown messages discusses the documentation change. The last messages cover a buildfarm failure on topminnow, which Thomas Munro traced to pg_walinspect rather than to the prefetch code.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow PostgreSQL to perform promote/pause/shutdown operations at end-of-the-wal when the recovery does not reach the recovery target
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal stops recovery from promoting at the end of available WAL when the recovery target was not reached, with a new setting (recovery_target_incomplete) to promote, pause or shut down instead. It later split into a second patch that refuses to start WAL replay when the recovery target lies before the restored backup's position, checked against pg_control.
precedents_retrieved.objection: David Steele found the start-point check incorrect: it uses the checkpoint in pg_control, but backup recovery starts from the backup_label checkpoint, and PITR can only start at backup end. The check would accept invalid targets in long backups and reject valid ones, and the last completed xid says little about commit order. He also noted that no consensus existed for the behaviour change, and returned the patch at the end of the CF.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
My point is that the
information you are working from (whatever checkpoint happens to be in
pg_control when recovery starts) is not sufficient for the task.  This
method is inaccurate and would disallow valid recovery scenarios.

precedents_retrieved.title: skip replication slot snapshot/map file removal during end-of-recovery checkpoint
precedents_retrieved.summary: Skip the enumeration and removal of logical replication snapshot (.snap) and mapping (map-) files during the end-of-recovery checkpoint, so the server becomes available sooner, and leave the files to the next regular checkpoint. A GUC could control this, with the current behavior as the default.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Nathan Bossart argued that skipping the files only at end of recovery does not solve the problem, because regular checkpoints stay slow and the shutdown or end-of-recovery checkpoint can still take a long time. He proposed moving these tasks out of checkpointing, which another thread was already discussing. The author agreed to handle the problem in that thread and withdrew this entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If
there are frequently many such files to delete and regular checkpoints
are taking longer, the shutdown/end-of-recovery checkpoint could still
take a while.  I think it would be better to separate these tasks from
checkpointing instead.

precedents_retrieved.title: Index Insert Prefetching
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add an index AM callback amprefetch, implemented for btree, that walks the inner pages of each index and prefetches the target leaf page before index tuples are inserted. The executor calls it for all indexes, and for whole COPY batches, behind a GUC enable_insert_prefetch.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas objected that the patch duplicates the btree descent code and its runtime work, and only helps index insertion. He suggested a general async execution model, where aminsert() returns a future that can wait on I/O. The author found the idea interesting but raised open questions about control flow and concurrency. The patch then stopped applying, and no new version appears before the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don't like this approach. It duplicates the tree-descend code, and it
also duplicates the work of descending the tree at runtime.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert recent changes related to handling of 2PC files at recovery
precedents_retrieved.authors: Michael Paquier, Alexander Korotkov, Simon Riggs
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert recent changes related to handling of 2PC files at recovery
Reverted commit(s): Fix handling of orphaned 2PC files in the future at recovery; Fix failures with incorrect epoch handling for 2PC files at recovery; Make use FullTransactionId in 2PC filenames; Speedup 2PC recovery by skipping two phase state files in normal path
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit reverts 8f67f994e8ea (down to v13) and c3de0f9eed38 (down to
v17), as these are proving to not be completely correct regarding two
aspects:
- In v17 and newer branches, c3de0f9eed38's check for epoch handling is
incorrect, and does not correctly handle frozen epochs.  A logic closer
to widen_snapshot_xid() should be used.  The 2PC code should try to
integrate deeper with FullTransactionIds, 5a1dfde8334b being not enough.
- In v13 and newer branches, 8f67f994e8ea is a workaround for the real
issue, which is that we should not attempt CLOG lookups without reaching
consistency.  This exists since 728bd991c3c4, and this is reachable with
ProcessTwoPhaseBuffer() called by restoreTwoPhaseData() at the beginning
of recovery.

Per discussion with Noah Misch.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add DB_IN_END_OF_RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT state for control file
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch stops the end-of-recovery checkpoint from setting the control file state to DB_SHUTDOWNING and then DB_SHUTDOWNED, which the author considered wrong. Two variants were posted: one adds a new state DB_IN_END_OF_RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT, and one keeps DB_IN_CRASH_RECOVERY or DB_IN_ARCHIVE_RECOVERY until DB_IN_PRODUCTION.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier argued that the current state is not incorrect, because an end-of-recovery checkpoint is a shutdown checkpoint and the code has relied on that for about 10 years. He said the change was not checked against other assumptions, such as unlogged relation reset needing a clean shutdown, and that it leaves an invalid minimum recovery point in DB_IN_ARCHIVE_RECOVERY. He added that it would make back-patching harder in a sensitive area, and the entry was closed after the thread went quiet.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This
patch would bring some extra visibility for something that's not
incorrect either on HEAD, as end-of-recovery checkpoints are the same
things as shutdown checkpoints.

precedents_retrieved.title: prefetching for nestloop / indexscan
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an ExecPrefetch executor callback so that a nested loop reads a batch of outer rows and asks a parameterized inner index scan to prefetch the matching heap pages. It is a small proof of concept limited to nestloop with an inner index scan, controlled by a new enable_nestloop_prefetch setting.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry because the patch was a quick experiment and he had no time to keep working on it. Before that, Andres Freund questioned the extra executor tree traversals and suggested passing multiple values down in one parameter, possibly as one ScalarArrayOps index scan. Peter Geoghegan supported that direction. The author agreed it looks like block nested loop join, which moves the work away from this design, and his cached-data benchmark showed about a 30% regression.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
But
the patch was just a quick & dirty experiment, I don't have time to work
on this right now.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P3] is the 2021 revert of the whole recovery prefetching feature, made for release-cycle timing. Its reason does not apply to a one-line bug fix in the later, committed prefetcher. The thread cites no earlier discussion of this bug, and the three replies (messages #2-#4) agree with the fix.

The patch adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object, psql behaviour or dump content, so it changes no user-facing contract; it only corrects recovery-end behaviour, and the backpatch through 15 fits normal bugfix practice. The open questions are outside this angle: whether to commit the TAP test, and how users can find clusters whose timeline history file got a wrong switch point.

The fix changes no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, protocol or exported struct. It clears one field in the prefetcher's private state, so backpatching to 15 creates no ABI or pg_upgrade problem. Release notes could tell users how to spot timeline history files with a wrong switch point that the bug has already written, but that does not argue against the fix. [P3] concerns the original feature's revert and does not apply to this bug fix.

The patch only clears a stale internal pointer in the recovery prefetcher. It adds no privilege, role, setting, view, error text or user-reachable path, and only the startup process runs this code. Recovery targets and maintenance_io_concurrency already require superuser or file access, so there is nothing to object to from a security angle.

This is a backpatched bugfix: one pointer reset, in the module that already owns that state. It adds no GUC, catalog change, API or hot-path work, and the cost of skipping it is wrong timeline history files and replay past the recovery target. [P3] reverted the original feature in 2021 and does not argue against fixing it now; whether to keep the TAP test is a test-level question and out of scope here.

This is a bug fix in recovery prefetcher state handling, so no existing feature, extension or setting meets the need. Setting recovery_prefetch = off avoids the bug but leaves it in place, so it is not an alternative. [P3] is about the original feature being reverted and does not apply.

This is a backpatched bug fix for a crash and a wrong timeline switch point in point-in-time recovery, which can then replay WAL past the recovery target, so the demand angle does not apply. Three people confirmed the bug and the fix (messages #2-#4); the open questions about the TAP test and the PANIC check are not demand concerns.
